prompt: A chained table doubles both its key count and bucket count under uniform hashing. With bounded-cost hashing and comparisons, what happens to expected unsuccessful-search comparisons?

options.text: They stay about the same because the load factor is unchanged.
options.explanation: An unsuccessful search scans its selected bucket, whose expected occupancy stays fixed.

options.text: They must double because the table has more keys.
options.explanation: The keys are spread over proportionally more buckets.

options.text: They become zero because all collisions disappear.
options.explanation: Constant average occupancy does not eliminate collisions.

options.text: They equal the fullest bucket on every search.
options.explanation: A typical selected bucket differs from the maximum bucket.

workedExample: The lookup inspects one bucket, not the entire table. Compare keys per bucket before and after growth. This is an expected model result, not a worst-case or adversarial guarantee.

prompt: An attacker can supply many keys with identical full hash values to a list-backed hash table. Which responses or conclusions are justified? Select all that apply.

options.text: Limit the amount of untrusted input processed.
options.explanation: This bounds exposure even if collisions occur.

options.text: Use an appropriate secret keyed hash for the relevant key types.
options.explanation: This makes precomputed collisions harder, subject to the function and threat model.

options.text: Doubling the bucket count necessarily separates these keys.
options.explanation: Identical full hash values still map together under the same bucket mapping rule.

options.text: Uniform-model expected performance may no longer describe these inputs.
options.explanation: The keys were deliberately chosen to collide.

workedExample: Identify why the expectation failed: the attacker controls the inputs. Resizing addresses occupancy but not equality of full hash values. Combine appropriate keyed hashing with resource limits and checks of which key types are actually covered.
